title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 304: The Mechanical Muse: AI and Art
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 304 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

The Mechanical Muse: Artificial Intelligence and Aesthetic Value

Paragraph 1. In May 2018, a simple-looking painting sold at a famous New York auction for $432,500. That price was forty times higher than people expected. Why did everyone talk about this picture? Instead of a human name at the bottom, the painting was signed with a math formula. An artificial intelligence (AI) computer program created the whole portrait after studying fifteen thousand old paintings from six hundred years of history.

Paragraph 2. Many tech fans thought computers had finally become creative like humans. However, philosopher Dr. Julian Barnes disagrees strongly. He explains how this AI system actually works. Two programs play a game against each other: one program builds digital pictures out of random noise, and the second program checks those pictures against real human art. After millions of tries, the computer gets very good at copying human style—but copying patterns is not real creativity.

Paragraph 3. Barnes says real art comes from personal human life and strong emotions. When Vincent van Gogh painted The Starry Night, he used paint to share deep sadness, wonder, and love. A computer program has no body, no life story, and zero feelings. It only moves colored dots around on a screen without understanding what pain or joy means.

Paragraph 4. Barnes also warns about two big problems with cheap AI art. First, if companies make endless free music and pictures by computer, real human artists may lose their jobs and money. Second, because AI only learns from old art, it keeps repeating styles from the past instead of breaking rules to invent truly fresh art.

groups.title: Questions 5–8
groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

steps: Đoạn 2: "...builds digital pictures out of random noise..."
Đoạn 3: "...no body, no life story, and zero feelings."
Đoạn 4: "...real human artists may lose their jobs and money."

q5.text: Why was the 2018 New York painting sale surprising?
options: A. It was painted over six hundred years ago.
B. It sold for a huge price even though a computer made it.
C. It was the largest oil painting ever sold at auction.
D. Famous human painters refused to look at it.

steps: Đoạn 1: Tranh do AI vẽ nhưng bán được $432,500, cao gấp 40 lần dự kiến.

q6.text: What does Dr. Julian Barnes believe about AI painting programs?
options: A. They are much smarter than famous museum directors.
B. They create brand-new art styles without any help.
C. They cannot learn how to copy older painting styles.
D. They only copy patterns and do not truly create.

q7.text: Why does the writer mention Van Gogh's painting The Starry Night?
options: A. To show that real human art expresses deep personal emotion
B. To prove that modern computers can paint like Van Gogh
C. To explain how auction houses set high painting prices
D. To argue that bright colours are easy for machines to copy

steps: Đoạn 3: Dùng tranh Van Gogh để minh họa nghệ thuật thật xuất phát từ cảm xúc sống của con người.

q8.text: Why could AI art harm future culture according to Paragraph 4?
options: A. It makes museum tickets too expensive for students.
B. It deletes old paintings from computer databases.
C. It keeps repeating old styles instead of inventing fresh ones.
D. It forces companies to hire thousands of extra painters.

steps: Đoạn 4: "...keeps repeating styles from the past instead of breaking rules to invent truly fresh art."
